get_citation.description: Get the reference PM2.5 Open Data asks you to cite when you use its data, or the one for its Anomaly Detection Framework (ADF), with a DOI link. No API key required.

@ARTICLE{7970115,
author={L. {Chen} and Y. {Ho} and H. {Lee} and H. {Wu} and H. {Liu} and H. {Hsieh} and Y. {Huang} and S. C. {Lung}},
journal={IEEE Access},
title={An Open Framework for Participatory PM2.5 Monitoring in Smart Cities},
year={2017},
volume={5},
number={},
pages={14441-14454},
abstract={As the population in cities continues to increase rapidly, air pollution becomes a serious issue from public health to social economy. Among all pollutants, fine particulate matters (PM2.5) directly related to various serious health concerns, e.g., lung cancer, premature death, asthma, and cardiovascular and respiratory diseases. To enhance the quality of urban living, sensors are deployed to create smart cities. In this paper, we present a participatory urban sensing framework for PM2.5 monitoring with more than 2500 devices deployed in Taiwan and 29 other countries. It is one of the largest deployment project for PM2.5 monitor in the world as we know until May 2017. The key feature of the framework is its open system architecture, which is based on the principles of open hardware, open source software, and open data. To facilitate the deployment of the framework, we investigate the accuracy issue of low-cost particle sensors with a comprehensive set of comparison evaluations to identify the most reliable sensor. By working closely with government authorities, industry partners, and maker communities, we can construct an effective eco-system for participatory urban sensing of PM2.5 particles. Based on our deployment achievements to date, we provide a number of data services to improve environmental awareness, trigger on-demand responses, and assist future government policymaking. The proposed framework is highly scalable and sustainable with the potential to facilitate the Internet of Things, smart cities, and citizen science in the future.},

readings.description: The readings or averages, oldest first. Empty when the sensor reported nothing in the period.

items.description: One reading, or the average of an hour's or a day's readings, in time order.

pm1.description: Average PM1 in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3).

pm10.description: Average PM10 in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3).

pm25_max.description: The highest PM2.5 reading in the row.

pm25_min.description: The lowest PM2.5 reading in the row.

readings.description: How many readings this row holds: 1 for a reading.

time.description: When: the reading's time, or the start of the hour or day it averages, ISO 8601 in the time zone asked for, e.g. '2024-07-19T10:00:00Z' or '2024-07-19T18:00:00+08:00'.

site_name.description: The name its host gave the sensor's site, often a school or a district and often in Chinese, e.g. '陽明-1(2020)'. Null when it has none.

summary.description: Across every reading counted: how many there are, the first and last time, and each measurement's lowest, highest and average. Null where no reading has the measurement.

first_time.description: The earliest reading's time, in UTC.

humidity_percent.description: The lowest, highest and average humidity.

mean.description: The average humidity, to two decimals.

last_time.description: The latest reading's time, in UTC.

pm1.description: The lowest, highest and average PM1.

mean.description: The average PM1, to two decimals.

mean.description: The average PM10, to two decimals.

pm25.description: The lowest, highest and average PM2.5.

mean.description: The average PM2.5, to two decimals.

temperature_c.description: The lowest, highest and average temperature.

time_zone.description: The time zone the day and the averages are counted in.

get_sensor_rankings.description: Get the Anomaly Detection Framework's ranking of PM2.5 sensors by the quality of their readings: every ranked sensor, one sensor's rank, or the sensors of one project, with each sensor's project and when it was ranked. No API key required.

parameters.description: Optional. One sensor to get the rank of, instead of every sensor. Its device id: an AirBox's is its MAC address, such as 74DA38F7C4B0. A link to the sensor's page on pm25.lass-net.org works too. Find sensors near a place and Get a project's latest readings report each sensor's id.
parameters.name: device_id

parameters.description: Optional. Only the sensors of this project. Cannot be combined with a Sensor. Pick from PM2.5 Open Data's projects or type one: airbox is the Edimax AirBoxes, the largest. List projects shows them all.
parameters.name: project

parameters.description: Optional. How many sensors to return at most, 1 to 1000. 100 by default.
parameters.name: limit

count.description: How many are returned here, at most Maximum sensors.

device_id.description: The sensor asked about, or null.

project.description: The project asked about, or null.

sensors.description: The ranked sensors, in the service's order.

items.description: One ranked sensor. ADF's answers carry the rank, when it was given and the project the sensor reports under, not a reading, so the measurements are null.

dashboard_url.description: The sensor's page on pm25.lass-net.org, which charts its readings: a link to put in a message.

date.description: The UTC day the reading was taken, YYYY-MM-DD. Get a sensor's readings takes it as its Date.

device_id.description: The sensor's device id, e.g. '74DA38F7C4B0'. An AirBox's is its MAC address. Get a sensor's latest reading and Get a sensor's readings take it.

fields.description: The record as PM2.5 Open Data sent it, field for field, including any measurement not named above under its LASS code (s_d0 is PM2.5, s_t0 temperature, s_h0 humidity).

humidity_percent.description: The relative humidity at the sensor, in percent. Low-cost PM2.5 sensors read high in very humid air.

latitude.description: Where the sensor is, as it reports it. Null when it has no position.

longitude.description: Where the sensor is, as it reports it. Null when it has no position.

minutes_old.description: How many minutes ago the reading was taken. An AirBox reports every five or six minutes, so a much larger number means it has gone quiet.

pm1.description: PM1 in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3). Null for sensors whose firmware reports PM2.5 only.

pm10.description: PM10 in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3). Null for sensors whose firmware reports PM2.5 only.

pm25.description: PM2.5, fine particles, in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3).

project.description: The project the sensor reports under, e.g. 'AirBox', 'LASS' or 'MAPS'. Null when the answer does not say.

rank.description: The sensor's rank, as the Anomaly Detection Framework gives it. Null when the answer carries none.

site_name.description: The name its host gave the sensor's site, often a school or a district and often in Chinese, e.g. '陽明-1(2020)'. Null when it has none.

temperature_c.description: The temperature at the sensor, in degrees Celsius.

time.description: When the reading was taken, ISO 8601 in UTC, e.g. '2024-07-19T10:17:01Z'.

total.description: How many sensors the answer holds.

updated_at.description: When PM2.5 Open Data made the answer, as it says it (ISO 8601 UTC), or null when it does not.

list_calibration_models.description: List the calibration models PM2.5 Open Data's Dynamic Calibration Framework (DCF) trained at air quality monitoring stations in Taiwan to correct low-cost sensors' PM2.5: each station's method, its inputs, how many days it learned from, the day it was trained, and its error before and after calibration. The latest models, one sensor type's, or a past day's. A station listed without a model comes back with its position only; Get a calibration model reads the last model trained there. No API key required.
list_calibration_models.display_str_template: List PM2.5 Open Data's calibration models.
list_calibration_models.name: list_calibration_models

parameters.description: Optional. Only the latest models for one type of low-cost sensor: the Plantower PMS5003 in the AirBox, or the Sensirion SPS30. Every type by default. Cannot be combined with a Date.
parameters.name: sensor

parameters.description: Optional. A past day's models instead of the latest: a date such as 2024-07-19.
parameters.name: date

date.description: The day asked for, or null for the latest.

models.description: The models, in the service's order.

config_url.description: A link to the model's configuration file, when the answer gives one.

consistency.description: The framework's consistency score for the model, as it reports it, or null.

date.description: The day the model was trained for, YYYY-MM-DD.

feature_code.description: The same inputs as the framework writes them, one letter each: P PM2.5, H hour, T temperature, R relative humidity, e.g. 'PHTR'.

features.description: What the model reads to calibrate a reading: pm25, hour (of the day), temperature and humidity.

fields.description: The model's record as PM2.5 Open Data sent it.

mae_calibrated.description: The model's mean absolute error against the station's own monitor, in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3). Null when the framework did not record it.

mae_raw.description: The uncalibrated sensor's mean absolute error against the same monitor, in micrograms per cubic metre (ug/m3), for comparison. Null when not given.

method.description: The regression method, as the framework names it, e.g. 'RandomForestRegressor' or 'GAM'.

method_name.description: The method in plain words, e.g. 'Random forest regression'.

model_url.description: A link to the model file (a scikit-learn .joblib), when the answer gives one.

sensor.description: The low-cost sensor the model calibrates: PMS5003 (the AirBox's) or SPS30. Null when the answer does not say.

site.description: The air quality monitoring station the model was trained at, e.g. 'wanhua'. Get a calibration model takes it.

training_days.description: How many days of readings the model learned from: 7, 14, 21 or 30.

version.description: When the model was built, e.g. '2024-07-19 00:01:12'.

sensor.description: The sensor type asked for, or null.

list_projects.description: List the projects PM2.5 Open Data files its sensors under, such as airbox for the Edimax AirBoxes and lass for the LASS community's own devices. Get a project's latest readings takes one. No API key required.
list_projects.name: list_projects

projects.description: The projects, in the service's order.

fields.description: Whatever else PM2.5 Open Data says about the project, as it says it.

id.description: The project's id, e.g. 'airbox'. Get a project's latest readings takes it.

name.description: The project's name, or its id when the answer gives no other.

description: Read PM2.5 Open Data, the open feed of the LASS PM2.5 project's low-cost air quality sensors, many of them AirBoxes in Taiwan: a sensor's latest reading or its last week as hourly averages, the sensors nearest a place, every sensor in a project, the Anomaly Detection Framework's flags and rankings, the Dynamic Calibration Framework's models, and how to cite it all. Readings are PM2.5, PM10 and PM1 with temperature and humidity. No account or API key required.
